standards.name: RDML (Real-time PCR Data Markup Language)
standards.abstract: RDML is a structured XML data standard for exchanging quantitative PCR (qPCR) and digital PCR (dPCR) data. It records experimental metadata (samples, targets, dyes, thermal cycling conditions, experimenters), per-reaction time-series fluorescence (amplification) and melting-curve data, and computed values (Cq, quantities, baseline metrics). RDML files are stored as an rdml_data.xml XML file inside a single PKZIP-compatible archive with extension .rdml/.rdm (or may be uncompressed .xml).

classification.rationale: RDML defines a formal XML schema enumerating named metadata elements and enumerated value types (i.e. a metadata table). The material provides explicit field names, types, and controlled values, so representing it as a metadata table is most information-dense.

file_container_and_name.name: RDML file container and name
file_container_and_name.descr: How the RDML XML should be packaged and named.
possible_values: .rdml (preferred) or .rdm archive containing rdml_data.xml; or uncompressed .xml file
file_container_and_name.evidence: The xml file containing the RDML compliant data should be stored in a file named rdml_data.xml. This file should be compressed using pkzip compatible compression into an archive. The archive can have any name, but instead of having the extension .zip it should have the extension .rdml (preferably) or .rdm. Archives ending in .rdml or .rdm should only contain one file, the file rdml_data.xml. Software should be able to read compressed .rdml or .rdm files as well as uncompressed .xml files.

file_encoding_and_conventions.name: XML encoding and separators
file_encoding_and_conventions.descr: Character encoding, newline and decimal separator conventions for RDML XML files.
file_encoding_and_conventions.evidence: The XML file should be encoded in UTF-8, \n should be used as newline character and a point "." as decimal separator.

purpose_description.name: Purpose / scope
purpose_description.descr: High-level purpose of RDML (what it stores and why).
purpose_description.evidence: The Real-time PCR Data Markup Language (RDML) is a structured and universal data standard for exchanging quantitative PCR (qPCR) data. The data standard should contain sufficient information to understand the experimental setup, re-analyse the data and interpret the results.

dataType.tar.name: data.tar (Target reference)
dataType.tar.evidence: TargetID - A reference to a target.

dataType.cq.name: data.cq (Quantification cycle)
dataType.cq.descr: Calculated fractional PCR cycle used for downstream quantification; uses special negative values to indicate NA.
dataType.cq.evidence: Quantification cycle - The calculated fractional PCR cycle used for downstream quantification. Negative values are used to express following conditions: Not Available: -1.0

dataType.excl.name: data.excl (Excluded flag / reason)
dataType.excl.descr: Indicates that an entry should not be evaluated; may contain string reason(s) separated by semicolons.
dataType.excl.evidence: Excluded - If present, this entry should not be evaluated. Do not set this element to false if this entry is valid, leave the entire element out instead. It may contain a string with reason for exclusion. Several reasons for exclusion should be separated by semicolons ";".

dataType.adp.name: data.adp (Amplification data points)
dataType.adp.descr: Amplification data points: the single data points measured during amplification; each point contains cycle, optional temperature, and fluorescence.
dataType.adp.evidence: Amplification data point - The single data points measured during amplification.

dpAmpCurveType.cyc_tmp_fluor.name: adp fields: cyc, tmp, fluor
dpAmpCurveType.cyc_tmp_fluor.descr: Per-amplification-point fields: cycle index, temperature (C), and raw fluorescence.
dpAmpCurveType.cyc_tmp_fluor.evidence: Cycle - The PCR cycle at which data point was collected. Temperature - The temperature in degrees Celsius at the time of measurement. Fluorescence - The fluorescence intensity measured.

dataType.mdp.name: data.mdp (Melting curve data points)
dataType.mdp.descr: Melting curve data points measured in melting analysis (temperature and fluorescence).
dataType.mdp.evidence: Melting curve data point - The single data points measured in the melting analysis.

dpMeltingCurveType.tmp_fluor.name: mdp fields: tmp, fluor
dpMeltingCurveType.tmp_fluor.descr: Per-melting-point fields: temperature (C) and raw fluorescence intensity (uncorrected).
dpMeltingCurveType.tmp_fluor.evidence: Columns: tmp (temperature in degrees Celsius at the time of measurement. Every point must have unique value.), fluor (fluorescence intensity measured without any correction (including baselining)).

dataType.bgFluor_bgFluorSlp_quantFluor.name: Background and quantification fluorescence fields
dataType.bgFluor_bgFluorSlp_quantFluor.descr: bgFluor: background fluorescence (y-intercept of baseline); bgFluorSlp: background fluorescence slope; quantFluor: fluorescence at threshold line.
dataType.bgFluor_bgFluorSlp_quantFluor.evidence: Background fluorescence - The y-intercept of the baseline trend based on the estimated background fluorescence. Background fluorescence slope - The slope of the baseline trend based on the estimated background fluorescence. The element should be absent to indicate a slope of 0.0; If this element is present without the bgFluor element it should be ignored. Quantification flourescence - The fluorescence value corresponding to the threshold line.

cqDetectionMethodType.name: cqDetectionMethodType (Cq detection method)
cqDetectionMethodType.descr: Controlled vocabulary for the method used to determine the Cq value.
cqDetectionMethodType.evidence:
The method used to determine the Cq value.
... <xs:enumeration value="automated threshold and baseline settings"/> <xs:enumeration value="manual threshold and baseline settings"/> <xs:enumeration value="second derivative maximum"/> <xs:enumeration value="other"/>

dataCollectionSoftwareType.name: dataCollectionSoftware (software name and version)
dataCollectionSoftwareType.descr: Name and version of software used to collect (and analyze) the data.
dataCollectionSoftwareType.evidence: Software name and version used to collect and analyze the data.

documentationType.name: documentation (shared text descriptions)
documentationType.descr: Reusable documentation elements that can be referenced by many samples, targets, or experiments.
documentationType.evidence: These elements should be used if the same description applies to many samples, targets or experiments.

quantityUnitType.name: quantityUnitType (quantity unit enumeration)
quantityUnitType.descr: Controlled list of units for quantities attached to samples/standards.
quantityUnitType.evidence: The unit the quantity. Can take values: cop copies per microliter, fold fold change, dil dilution (10 would mean 1:10 dilution), nMol nanomol per microliter, ng nanogram per microliter, other other unit (must be linear, no exponents or logarithms allowed)

id_strings_uniqueness.name: id strings: uniqueness and human-readable requirement
id_strings_uniqueness.descr: IDs in RDML should be unique human-readable short names provided by the user (not random strings).
id_strings_uniqueness.evidence: All id strings in the file should be unique short names as provided by the user. Do not use random generated strings as ids, as they should be displayed to the user for example to identify different samples.

standards.notes: This extraction focuses on the metadata fields and file-format notes present in the RDML schema and documentation. The RDML resources include a full XML schema (XSD) with many more types and elements; the listed fields are core/common elements with explicit schema documentation quoted verbatim.
